lesson.menu_desc: Twelve months of an account in twenty minutes, for an executive who has never met you: who you are, what changed, which number matters -- relative clauses
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 25 -- The Business Review: twelve months for an executive who has never met you
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Patrícia Xavier Lima Iwashita | Lesson 25 -- The Business Review
lesson.grammar_point: relative clauses (who / which / that / whose / where)

listenings.text: Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. A few things about tomorrow's business review at Northwind. Richard Moore is the new executive sponsor who took over in February, so he has never met you and he has never seen our numbers. He is a man whose calendar is full from eight to eight, so you will get twenty minutes, not an hour. Open with the headline, which is simple: usage has come back on every team. Then give him three numbers, not ten. The first is the footprint. Last year we were in three teams, and today we are in six, including finance. The second is the time that the warehouse team saves on every order. The third is the benchmark, which shows that Northwind is doing better than similar companies. Do not explain the product. Richard is not the person who uses it. He is the person who pays for it.

Patrícia, it is David. A quick tip about Richard, because I have worked with him for six years. Richard is a person who reads the last slide first. He wants to know the decision that you need from him, so put it at the top. He also hates words that he cannot measure. If you say better, he will ask better than what. If you say faster, he will ask how many minutes. And one more thing. Richard came from a company where they consolidated five tools into one, so he likes vendors who make things simpler, not bigger. Tell him that our platform replaced two spreadsheets and an old reporting tool, which is true, and he will listen. Keep it short, and please do not read the slides to him.
